Artificing Kit: Downtime: roll Occult, Nature, or Technology Education. The GM may impose a Boon or Bane based on the likelihood of finding Shards. Find one Shard per success. Roll a d6 per Shard for its color: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, or violet, in that order.
Artisan Kit: Choose a research or innovation topic when buying this kit. When using an Exertion Modifier on relevant Innovation or Research downtime, reroll dice that show a 1.
Basic Pokefood: Expend with Throw to land in an empty space. Enemy Pokémon within 3 m make a Tough Focus check (CR 3). If any fail, one uses its next Standard action to move to the space and eat the bait. The GM can lower the CR for obvious traps or repeated attempts.
Typed Pokefood: Choose a type at creation. Use the Basic Pokefood bait rules: Throw into an empty space, then enemies within 3 m roll Focus (CR 3). Pokémon of the chosen type take a Bane. If any fail, one uses its next Standard action to move there and eat.
Climbing Kit: While carried, climb vertical surfaces without a skill check. If equipped as a weapon-slot item, also ignore movement penalties from vertical surfaces that count as Slow Terrain.
First Aid Kit: With Adept Medicine Education, spend around five minutes on an Extended action to cure a physical affliction. If carried at the end of a combat scene, the user and allies recover three HP ticks. Extra kits or Mender increase the recovery by one tick each.
Hazard Bag: Choose a Hazard-keyword attack when creating the bag. Expend the bag to use that attack immediately as if you knew it.
Ingredients (Basic): Specify the category this material can craft. Each unit spent covers up to $100 of crafting cost in that category.
Ingredients (Unique): Specify the crafting category. Each unit covers up to $500 of crafting cost. A project made entirely with this ingredient may inherit a property of the material, subject to GM approval.
Pokedex: While carried, gain a Boon on Pokémon Education checks from Analyze. As an Extended action, scan a Pokémon within 10 m for one minute to get basic information.
Pokepuff: Expend to give a Pokémon +1d6 the next time it is Socialized with during downtime. This die can exceed the normal six-die limit, and only one Pokepuff can affect a Pokémon at a time. It also works as Basic Pokefood bait.
Sleeping Bag: Provides a normal night's rest for one person on a journey.
Tent: Provides a normal night's rest for up to two people on a journey.
Tool Kit: Choose an action at creation. The kit provides the tools and grants a Boon to related skill checks outside downtime.
Trap Set: Choose the intended target and trigger effect at creation. Expend during downtime to set the trap. The GM may use a Luck roll for success or an opposed check to see if the target detects it.
Travel Set: Choose a crafting category at creation. While carried, it enables crafting in that category on a journey. Spend Ingredients equal to the crafting cost.
Air Balloon: Small Pokémon only. While equipped, gain Flier and immunity to attacks with the Groundsource keyword.
Artisan Pack: As an Extended action, designate a Small item with GM approval. While equipped, you can treat that item as a Resource. Contents are inaccessible while the pack is impaired.
Bardic Instrument: Choose two attacks for a Medium instrument, or three for a Large instrument. While equipped, you may use them: Heal Bell, Sing, Screech, Sonic Boom, Supersonic, or Metal Sound.
Berserk Belt: While equipped, when your damaging attack faints an enemy, increase either Attack or Special Attack by one combat stage.
Blessed Relic: While equipped, gain +2 on save checks.
Cargo Bag: Pokémon equipment. Adds four Inventory slots for cargo. An adjacent Trainer may equip or use contents as their own. A Small Pokémon cannot carry Large items in the bag.
Covert Cloak: While equipped, incoming attacks take a −2 penalty to their effect ranges.
Disguise: While equipped, a Small disguise gives a Bane to checks to see through it. A Large disguise also grants +1d6 to skill checks relating to the false identity. Price varies by complexity.
Dodge Scarf: While equipped, gain Evasion equal to your Tier Level. Spend a Reaction and Movement action to treat this bonus as uncapped until the start of your next turn.
Eject Module: Pokémon only. After resolving a hit, a conscious holder may recall itself as a free reaction. Its Trainer may send a replacement Pokémon to the same space as a Free action.
Fine Weapon: Requires Expert in the qualifying skill. Choose two Weapon Keywords. Medium: up to two Novice and one Advanced attack. Large: up to two Novice and two Advanced attacks. Use Create Weapon to choose eligible attacks.
Focus Sash: While equipped, gain Endure without using an Attack List slot. Using Endure resets your positive combat stages to their default values.
Heavy Backpack: While equipped, adds six Inventory slots for Small items. Its contents are inaccessible while impaired. Total Inventory capacity is capped at 12.
Jewelry: A small equipped accessory. The GM may assign a special effect at creation and price it accordingly. Plain jewelry provides no mechanical benefit.
Large Gadget: The GM sets the gadget's purpose and effect at creation. Its reusable benefit applies while equipped.
Legendary Weapon: Requires Master in the qualifying skill. Choose two Weapon Keywords. Medium: up to two Novice, one Advanced, and one Master attack. Large: up to two of each. Use Create Weapon to choose eligible attacks.
Light Backpack: While equipped, adds two Inventory slots for Small items. Its contents are inaccessible while impaired. Total Inventory capacity is capped at 12.
Lucky Charm: While equipped, reroll natural 1s on Accuracy rolls.
Pokemon Saddle: With GM approval, a Medium or larger Pokémon can equip this to gain Mountable. If impaired, riders are dismounted and become Tripped unless they pass a Standard Acrobatics check (CR 2).
Quick Claw: While equipped, when you activate Dash on an attack, enemies not targeted by that attack cannot use Reactions against it.
Ranger Styler: Outside combat, turn a Pokémon eligible for capture into a Companion. While equipped, spend a Standard action to target an enemy within 5 m. Roll Command or Charm opposed by Focus. On a win choose Guard Break (next incoming attack ignores Evasion), Pacify (its damaging attacks are resisted one extra step on its next turn), or Restrain (Trap it with yourself or an ally, or halve its Movement until the end of its next turn).
Razor Claw: While equipped, your melee attacks gain Pass.
Revenge Band: While equipped, gain +3 Damage Base on attacks against enemies that targeted you last round.
Seed Bag: During downtime, load or replace up to three options. While equipped and unimpaired, use the loaded attacks as known attacks: Leech Seed, Burn Powder, Mystic Powder, Sleep Powder, Stun Spore, or Poison Powder.
Simple Weapon: Requires Adept in the qualifying skill. Choose one Weapon Keyword. Medium: up to two Novice attacks. Large: up to two Novice and one Advanced attack. Use Create Weapon to choose eligible attacks.
Small Gadget: A one-use tool with a GM-defined effect. If it grants a Capability, such as through Tech Researcher, the benefit lasts until the end of the session or scene, whichever is later.
Stat Booster: Choose a stat other than HP at creation. While equipped, set that stat's default combat stage to +1.
Status Guard: Choose an affliction at creation. While equipped, the holder is immune to that affliction from ordinary sources. Against a boss inflicting it, make a TN 8 save to avoid it.
Stylish Clothes: Choose a skill at creation. When equipped, gain +1d6 to its checks outside downtime, up to 6d6. A Large set may also grant a Specialty and a Boon on checks within it. A Small set costs $1,500 and a Large set costs $3,000.
Survival Clothes: The GM chooses a terrain when purchased or crafted. While equipped, gain Naturewalk for that terrain.
Training Weapon: No qualifying skill rank or Weapon Keywords. Medium: up to one Novice attack. Large: up to two Novice attacks. Use Create Weapon to select attacks appropriate to the weapon.
Type Augmentor: Choose a type at creation. While equipped, spend a Swift action to change a damaging attack you know to that type for the rest of the scene.
Type Booster: Choose a type at creation. While equipped, damaging attacks of that type gain Smite.
Type Brace: Choose a type at creation. While equipped, resist attacks of that type by one additional damage step.
Basic Baggage: Essential travel baggage for carrying personal belongings. Takes no Inventory slot and does not grant extra capacity.
Clothing: Essential everyday clothing. Takes no Inventory slot. Specialized clothing uses its own item rules.
Collection Jars: Essential containers for gathering and transporting samples. Take no Inventory slots.
Lighter: Essential ignition tool for ordinary fires and lamps. Takes no Inventory slot.
Party Pokéballs: Occupied Poké Balls for active party members count as Essentials and take no Inventory slots. The default party limit is three Pokémon. Empty Poké Balls use slots.
Phone: Essential communication device. Takes no Inventory slot.
Rations: Ordinary travel food is Essential and takes no Inventory slots.
Towels: Ordinary travel towels are Essential and take no Inventory slots.
Water: Ordinary drinking water is Essential and takes no Inventory slots.
Water Filter: Essential travel tool for obtaining drinkable water where suitable. Takes no Inventory slot.
Ability Capsule: Choose an ability at creation. Expend on a Pokémon you own so it can choose that ability next time it is eligible to learn one, in place of a natural option. The GM may define an attack version.
Book: The GM chooses a subject, associated skill, and research target number. Complete the downtime study project to gain the information or lasting benefit assigned to the book.
Companion Ball: As an Extended action, bind one Pokémon you own. While carried, it counts as a party member beyond the usual limit but cannot enter combat. Only one Companion Ball can be carried at a time.
Elemental Catalyst: Choose a type at creation. Expend on a willing Pokémon to turn it into a Type Shift of that type. Add the type to a single-type Pokémon or replace an existing type, following Type Shift rules.
Elemental Enchantment: Choose an attack at creation. Expend to add it to an Equipment item, which can hold up to two enchanted attacks. Its wearer can use the attack while equipped and can treat a damaging one as a Weapon Attack.
Elemental Essence: Choose a type at creation. The Trainer who expends it gains Elemental Affinity for that type without using a Talent slot.
Evolution Stone: Expend on a Pokémon within 10 levels of an available evolution. It evolves and learns a Tier 1 Tutor Attack.
Fossil: Choose a species at creation. A character knowledgeable in paleontology can complete a TN 100 Pokémon Education Research project and use suitable equipment to restore it. It hatches at level 1 and may be Rock Type Shifted if not already Rock.
Gemstone: Loot with no inherent effect. Suggested sale prices: $1,000 common, $3,000 rare, $5,000 very rare.
Gym Badge: The GM chooses its type and effect. The sample badge adds Tier Level to Accuracy with attacks of its type while equipped. During Training downtime, teach one Pokémon a matching eligible Tutor Attack.
Harnessed Attack: The GM assigns an attack. Expend as a Standard action, or Swift with its Versatile option, to use it. For damage, you may use twice your Tier Value as the offensive stat. A GM-approved equipment version trades consumable use for once per scene.
Mega Stone: Choose a species and an ability from its Dex list. The matching equipped Pokémon may Mega Evolve as a Swift action, gaining one combat stage in a chosen stat and the ability until scene end. It cannot shift on a turn when it already used a damaging attack or use one after shifting that turn.
Pokemon Egg: Track Nurture Points. Roll 2d10 at the end of each game day and as a nurturing Downtime action, or 4d10 with Expert Pokémon Education. At 100 points, the egg hatches into a level 5 Pokémon. Price depends on rarity and special qualities.
Rare Candy: Expend to grant a Trainer or Pokémon +3 SP and the benefits of being targeted with a Training downtime action.
Terastral Crystal: Choose a type at creation. Once per scene as a Swift action, the equipped Pokémon may replace its current types with that type until scene end. Battle List attacks matching a lost type may shift to the new type.
Tutor Record: The GM assigns a tier or type. Expend to teach a Pokémon a matching Tutor Attack from its list for which it meets the tutoring rules.
Z Crystal: Choose a type. Once per scene as a Standard action, prime the equipped Pokémon to double the Damage Base of its next damaging hit of that type. Twice per scene as a Swift action, prime its next damaging attack of that type with Smite and Spirit Surge.
